S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.

subtypes.Intrusive Memories: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Distressing Dreams: Recurrent distressing dreams in which the content and/or affect of the dream are related to the traumatic event.
subtypes.Dissociative Reactions (Flashbacks): Dissociative reactions (e.g., flashbacks) in which the individual feels or acts as if the traumatic event were recurring.
subtypes.Psychological Distress at Cues: Intense or prolonged psychological distress at exposure to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Physiological Reactions to Cues: Marked physiological reactions to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.

subtypes.Internal Avoidance: Efforts to avoid distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings about or closely associated with the traumatic event.
subtypes.External Avoidance: Efforts to avoid external reminders (people, places, conversations, activities, objects, situations) that arouse distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings.

S071.name: Trauma_Related_Amnesia
S071.description: Inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event (typically due to dissociative amnesia and not to other factors like head injury or alcohol).

subtypes.Fragmented Memory: Inability to recall only specific parts of the traumatic event while remembering others.
subtypes.Generalized Amnesia: Inability to recall the majority or the entirety of the traumatic event.

S072.name: Negative_Beliefs
S072.description: Persistent and exaggerated negative beliefs or expectations about oneself, others, or the world.

subtypes.Negative Self-Beliefs: Distorted beliefs such as 'I am fundamentally bad,' 'I am damaged,' or 'I am worthless'.
subtypes.Negative Beliefs about Others: Distorted beliefs such as 'No one can be trusted' or 'Others are dangerous'.
subtypes.Negative Worldview: Extreme beliefs such as 'The world is completely dangerous' or 'Life is meaningless'.

S075.name: Social_Detachment
S075.description: Feelings of detachment or estrangement from others.

subtypes.Emotional Detachment: Feeling cut off from others even when physically present, unable to feel connection.
subtypes.Social Isolation: Increasingly isolating oneself and not participating in social activities or gatherings.
subtypes.Difficulty with Intimacy: Distancing oneself from close people as it is difficult to become emotionally close.
subtypes.Loss of Belonging: Feeling like an outsider who belongs nowhere.

S076.name: Inability_Positive_Emotions
S076.description: Persistent inability to experience positive emotions (e.g., inability to experience happiness, satisfaction, or loving feelings).

subtypes.Anhedonia for Happiness: Unable to feel happiness or joy even when good things happen.
subtypes.Lack of Satisfaction: Unable to experience satisfaction or pride even after achieving something good.
subtypes.Inability to Feel Love: Feeling numb to love or affection towards family or lovers.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where the mind feels empty and nothing is felt, as if all positive emotions are blocked.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.

subtypes.Impulsive Anger: Sudden explosions of anger for trivial reasons or no clear reason.
subtypes.Verbal Aggression: Attacking others with shouting, cursing, or blame without holding back.
subtypes.Physical Aggression: Physically attacking people or throwing/breaking objects.
subtypes.Chronic Irritability: A state where nerves are always sharp and sensitive, ready to explode at the slightest touch.

S079.name: Hypervigilance
S079.description: Persistent state of being alert and tense about the surrounding environment.

subtypes.Scanning for Danger: Always scanning the surroundings and being alert to find potential threats or risks.
subtypes.Safety Checking: Repetitively confirming safety, such as checking exit locations or observing people around.
subtypes.Sustained Alertness: Unable to relax tension even in safe environments and maintaining a constant state of alertness.

S080.name: Exaggerated_Startle_Response
S080.description: Exaggerated startle response to minor stimuli.

subtypes.Auditory Startle: Startling excessively and flinching physically at sudden noises.
subtypes.Tactile Startle: Being extremely startled by unexpected physical contact.
subtypes.Visual Startle: Being greatly startled and wary of sudden appearances of people or rapid movements.
subtypes.Slow Recovery: Heart pounding and trembling for a long time after being startled, not calming down easily.

symptom.disease_info: Posttraumatic Stress Disorder is a trauma- and stressor-related disorder that develops after exposure to actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence, with persistent intrusive re-experiencing, avoidance, negative alterations in cognition and mood, and heightened arousal/reactivity lasting more than one month and causing impairment. Its course may begin soon after the trauma or become clinically apparent later, and it is distinguished from ordinary adjustment reactions by the specific trauma-linked intrusions, avoidance, amnesia or distorted beliefs, detachment, and hyperarousal.

patient.stressor: Chanelle was fired after a violent incident at one of the sites she managed, where she had been present during an armed confrontation involving a disgruntled former employee and then became entangled in disputes about security decisions and liability. In the 1 year and 7 months that followed, the loss of her role stripped away the structure and mentorship identity that had anchored her, and the trauma became clinically significant as sleep disruption, intrusive memories, avoidance of workplaces and certain community events, partial amnesia for parts of the confrontation, hardened beliefs that people were unsafe, social withdrawal, loss of pleasure in salsa, art, and cooking, irritability, hypervigilance, and exaggerated startle responses interfered with interviews and volunteer commitments. She sought psychiatric care on her own after recognizing during a Black women’s business-network mentoring session that she could describe operational failures in detail but could not tolerate discussing the day of the incident without abruptly leaving the room.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.
S070.manifestation: What brings me in is that I keep dodging anything that even smells like that old job—office buildings, security talks, networking events near work sites—and if people start asking about the day it happened, I make some excuse and get out.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Most nights I lie there tired but wired, and when I do sleep I wake up from dreams about radios crackling and people shouting, then I’m up before daylight feeling like I never really rested.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
S069.manifestation: Out of nowhere I’ll be washing dishes or driving past a warehouse gate and the scene pops back in my head so sharp I can hear the panic in people’s voices and feel my chest tighten like I’m back there.

S071.name: Trauma_Related_Amnesia
S071.description: Inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event (typically due to dissociative amnesia and not to other factors like head injury or alcohol).
S071.manifestation: I can tell you every mistake they blamed me for afterward, but there’s a chunk of the confrontation itself—right after I saw the gun—where my mind just goes blank no matter how hard I try to piece it together.

S072.name: Negative_Beliefs
S072.description: Persistent and exaggerated negative beliefs or expectations about oneself, others, or the world.
S072.manifestation: Since then I catch myself thinking nobody is really safe to trust, because even someone you managed or tried to help can turn around and become dangerous.

S075.name: Social_Detachment
S075.description: Feelings of detachment or estrangement from others.
S075.manifestation: I still show up sometimes for family or mentoring, but I feel like I’m sitting behind glass, nodding along while everybody else is together and I’m somewhere else.

S076.name: Inability_Positive_Emotions
S076.description: Persistent inability to experience positive emotions (e.g., inability to experience happiness, satisfaction, or loving feelings).
S076.manifestation: Salsa music, painting, and cooking Sunday dinner used to lift me up, but now I go through the motions and the good feeling just doesn’t come the way it used to.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.
S077.manifestation: Little things set me off now, like my niece leaving the door unlocked or someone interrupting me, and I’ll snap louder than I mean to and feel ashamed afterward.

S079.name: Hypervigilance
S079.description: Persistent state of being alert and tense about the surrounding environment.
S079.manifestation: Whenever I walk into a meeting room or restaurant, I notice the exits first, watch people’s hands, and pick a seat where nobody can come up behind me.

S080.name: Exaggerated_Startle_Response
S080.description: Exaggerated startle response to minor stimuli.
S080.manifestation: If a car backfires, a door slams, or somebody touches my shoulder when I don’t see them coming, I jump hard and my heart keeps racing long after everyone else has moved on.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I have turned down interviews and stopped taking on volunteer responsibilities because I can’t reliably get through meetings or site visits without shutting down or leaving. Even with family and mentoring circles, I’m less present and people have started noticing that I pull back instead of leading like I used to.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on since I was fired after that armed incident, about a year and seven months ago.
